scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): largely accepts welfare as the better indicator while granting that achievements contribute; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Nations can be judged by their great works or by the lives of their ordinary people.
Some people claim that the general welfare of a nation's people is a better sign of greatness than the achievements of its rulers, artists, or scientists.
I largely agree with this claim, though I believe achievements still contribute to a nation's greatness.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why welfare is the better indicator

sentences.text: First, the general welfare of the people is indeed a better indicator of greatness.
A nation may produce dazzling achievements while the majority of its people remain poor.
For example, a country with brilliant scientists but hungry citizens has failed its most basic duty.
This shows that achievements mean little if ordinary lives do not improve.
Welfare reaches every citizen, while great achievements may benefit only a small elite.
Any nation that cares for all its people has fulfilled its deepest purpose.
To this extent, welfare is rightly the better measure of greatness.
Second, however, achievements should not be dismissed as a sign of greatness.
Great works of art and science often improve the welfare of the people themselves.
Consider how medical discoveries lengthen lives or how great art enriches an entire culture.
Such achievements are frequently a cause of welfare rather than something separate from it.
Nations that value learning and creativity also tend to grow healthier and wealthier.
Achievements can give a people pride and a strong, shared sense of identity.
Welfare and achievement, then, work together rather than against each other.
In conclusion, the welfare of the people is the better indicator of a nation's greatness.
But achievements matter too, since they often raise that welfare and enrich the culture.
A truly great nation directs its finest achievements toward the welfare of all its people.
